title: Bible ↔ Tim/Son Reader Manifest
status: functional reader manifest; WEB loaded on demand from public-domain upstream
purpose: Drive a side-by-side Bible reader in which the biblical text remains an immutable primary-source layer and Tim/Son chronology, overlap profiles, countertexts and source direction appear in separate annotation panes.

source.loading_mode: upstream-on-demand until local vendoring is complete

reading_modes.label: Bible order
reading_modes.description: Read the profiled passages in canonical book/chapter order while project annotations follow beside them.

reading_modes.label: Tim/Son chronology
reading_modes.description: Read overlaps by project-side date to see how the biblical vocabulary and structures accumulated.

reading_modes.label: Most explicit
reading_modes.description: Prioritize passages/titles explicitly invoked on the project side.

reading_modes.label: Most independent
reading_modes.description: Prioritize project structures that clearly predate the later archive comparison.

reading_modes.label: Most textually dense
reading_modes.description: Prioritize coherent biblical units containing many distinct project-relevant functions.

reading_modes.label: Most role-faithful
reading_modes.description: Prioritize comparisons that preserve who does what rather than collapsing actors.

reading_modes.label: Most sequence-faithful
reading_modes.description: Prioritize multi-step transformation/relationship sequences rather than shared nouns.

reading_modes.label: Best context survival
reading_modes.description: Prioritize comparisons that remain useful after countertexts and literary context are considered.

integrity_rules: Scripture and project interpretation must render in visibly separate columns/layers.
Never edit the WEB wording to make an overlap appear stronger.
Do not infer missing verse precision from a chapter-level citation; load the cited chapter/range as cited.
A project-side date and an archive discovery date are separate facts.
Direct biblical borrowing can score high on explicitness while low on temporal/feature independence.
Side-by-side presentation is comparative annotation, not a claim that the Bible predicts Tim/Son.
Every high-value card must display a limiting difference or route to a countertext when one exists.
Original-language and reception-history claims live in separate research owners and may not overwrite the English source text.
